questions.a: Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon.

questions.q: Why was David not able to build a house for the name of Yahweh?
questions.a: David was not able to build a house for the name of Yahweh because he led his soldiers to fight many wars against his enemies.
Yahweh told David, “Your son whom I will set on the throne will build a temple for my name.”

questions.q: What did Solomon ask Hiram to do?
questions.a: Solomon asked Hiram to command his servants to cut cedars from Lebanon for him.

questions.q: What did Hiram do when he heard Solomon’s words?
questions.a: Hiram rejoiced greatly and said, “May Yahweh be blessed today.”

questions.q: Did Hiram do what Solomon asked him to do?
questions.a: Yes, Hiram sent word saying, “I will do all you desire concerning the timber of cedar and cypress.”

questions.q: What would Hiram’s servants do with the trees?
questions.a: Hiram’s servants brought the trees down from Lebanon to the sea, where they were made into rafts to sail the wood to the place that Solomon indicated.

questions.q: What did Hiram want Solomon to do for him?
questions.a: Hiram desired that Solomon would supply food for his men.

questions.q: What food did Solomon give to Hiram?
questions.a: Solomon gave Hiram 20,000 measures of wheat and 20 measures of pure oil olive oil every year.

questions.q: Was there peace between Hiram and Solomon?
questions.a: Yes, there was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a covenant.

questions.q: How many forced laborers did Solomon have out of Israel?
questions.a: Solomon had 30,000 forced laborers out of Israel.

questions.q: Who did Solomon put over all of the forced laborers?
questions.a: Solomon put Adoniram over all of the forced laborers.

questions.q: Did Solomon have men who supervised all of the workers?
questions.a: Yes, Solomon had 3,300 chief officers who were over the work and supervised the workers.

questions.q: What did the workers quarry for the foundation of the house of Yahweh?
questions.a: The workers quarried large stones for the foundation of the house of Yahweh.

commentary.text: Verses 1–9 Here is Solomon's design to build a temple. There is no adversary, no Satan, so the word is; no instrument of Satan to oppose it, or to divert from it. Satan does all he can, to hinder temple work. When there is no evil abroad, then let us be ready and active in that which is good, and get forward. Let God's promises quicken our endeavours. And all outward skill and advantages should be made serviceable to the interests of Christ's kingdom.—If Tyre supplies Israel with craftsmen, Israel will supply Tyre with corn, Eze 27:17. Thus, by the wise disposal of Providence, one country has need of another, and is benefitted by another, that there may be dependence on one another, to the glory of God.

The temple was chiefly built by the riches and labour of Gentiles, which typified their being called into the church. Solomon commanded, and they brought costly stones for the foundation. Christ, who is laid for a Foundation, is a chosen and precious Stone. We should lay our foundation firm, and bestow most pains on that part of our religion which lies out of the sight of men. And happy those who, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, for a habitation of God through the Spirit. Who among us will build in the house of the Lord?
